quickstartupguide.timeLayoutIntro: A time layout defines each day's periods (morning reading, first period, second period, etc.) and forms the framework of your schedule.
quickstartupguide.timeLayoutStepAdd: Open the time layout editor and click "Add period" to create a new period
quickstartupguide.timeLayoutStepReorder: Drag periods to reorder them and set each period's start and end time
quickstartupguide.timeLayoutStepSubjects: Optional: after linking a subject list, set a default subject for each period
quickstartupguide.timeLayoutStepSave: Save and note the time layout name; you'll need it when creating an archive
quickstartupguide.subjectsIntro: A subject list (subject library) defines the courses offered at your school; archives (schedules) reference subjects from it.
quickstartupguide.subjectsStepPreset: A new subject list is pre-filled with 13 standard subjects (Chinese, math, English, etc.)
quickstartupguide.subjectsStepEdit: In the list you can edit a subject's name, short name, teacher, and whether it is an outdoor class
quickstartupguide.subjectsStepAdd: To add other subjects, click "Add subject"
quickstartupguide.subjectsStepSave: Save and note the subject list name; you'll need it when creating an archive
quickstartupguide.archiveIntro: An archive is a schedule in ClassIsland: it combines a time layout and a subject list to arrange classes by weekday.
quickstartupguide.archiveStepSelect: After creating an archive, first select a "Time layout" and a "Subject list"
quickstartupguide.archiveStepFill: Click a subject name on the left to select it, then click a cell on the right to fill it in
quickstartupguide.archiveStepSlots: Each cell corresponds to a period; different periods can hold different courses
quickstartupguide.archiveStepSave: Once saved, the archive is ready to be linked to a class
quickstartupguide.createClassAndLink: Create a class and link resources
quickstartupguide.classIntro: A class is the basic unit for resource dispatch. Each class can have its own archive, time layout, and policy.
quickstartupguide.classStepCreate: Create a class and enter its name (e.g. "Grade 10 Class 1")
quickstartupguide.classStepLink: Select "Archive", "Time layout", "Subject list", and "Policy" from the drop-down lists
quickstartupguide.classStepHint: If all the resources above have been created, they should all be selectable here.
quickstartupguide.classStepSave: Saving completes the class links and lets you generate a dispatch configuration.
quickstartupguide.dispatchIntro: Final step: generate the configuration file and place it on the ClassIsland device to load it automatically.
quickstartupguide.dispatchStepList: Open "Class list" and click the "Dispatch" button for the relevant class to copy its configuration.
quickstartupguide.dispatchStepDetail: Or open the class details and copy/download the configuration file from the "Deployment" card
quickstartupguide.dispatchStepPlace: Place the configuration file in the ClassIsland application folder on the classroom computer
quickstartupguide.dispatchStepJoin: Launch ClassIsland and click "Join management" in Settings to apply it

extra.refreshHint: Refresh this page when done to continue to the next step

extra.introP1: This is an unofficial ClassIsland central-control platform. It lets you dispatch various configuration resource files to ClassIsland installations in bound classrooms from this web page, saving time on repetitive configuration.
extra.introP2: Built for AV directors who have rolled out ClassIsland across their school and need to configure each class quickly, the platform provides centralized management of schedules and policies.
extra.introP3: AV committee members can manage classes centrally and dispatch configurations remotely. Students only need to restart CI after receiving a notification in the classroom — no interaction with the wired whiteboard required.
